insights.headline: Gold holds near $3,900 after one-year low; silver faces sixth deficit year
insights.summary: Spot gold steadied near $3,900 an ounce after touching a one-year low, with bargain hunting offset by a firm dollar at a 19-month high and rising bets on a December Fed hike. The Silver Institute expects the silver market to run a 35-million-ounce deficit in 2026, its sixth straight shortfall, while Indian jewellery demand by volume fell 20% in the September quarter. US producer prices due at 19:00 IST are the next test for rate expectations.
points: Spot gold rose 1% to $3,915.31 an ounce on Friday after hitting its lowest since October 2025 on Thursday, but is down 3.5% so far this week.
Silver rose 1% to $50.49 an ounce, also headed for a weekly decline; palladium gained 2.1% to $1,014.50.
Markets see an 89% chance of a 25-basis-point December Fed hike and 11% for a 50-point move, after hot October US inflation and hawkish Fed remarks.
MCX December gold held near Rs 1.39 lakh per 10 g and silver near Rs 1.82 lakh per kg, with the rupee near 94 per dollar.
Silver is set for a sixth straight annual deficit of 35 million ounces in 2026, and Indian jewellery demand by volume fell 20% in Q2.

brief.headline: Gold near one-year low as Fed hike bets harden
brief.summary: Gold held near $3,883 after a one-year-low settle, with MCX gold near Rs 1.39 lakh per 10 g as a firm dollar weighed.

bullets.text: Hot October US CPI lifted December hike bets, pushing the dollar to a 19-month high and Treasury yields up, Reuters reports.
In India, MCX gold and silver tracked the global slide, while Diwali demand stayed firm as prices fell, with gold purchases up 30%.
Watch today: US producer prices at 19:00 IST, after October CPI came in hot at 0.4%.

trending.title: Gold rebounds from one-year low but heads for weekly loss
trending.summary: Spot gold rose 1% to $3,915.31 on Friday as bargain hunting followed Thursday's slide to its lowest since October 2025, but stayed down 3.5% for the week.

trending.title: December hike bets harden after hot CPI
trending.summary: October CPI rose 0.4% with core up 0.3%, and Fed officials signalled further rises may be needed; markets price an 89% chance of a 25-basis-point December hike and 11% for 50.

trending.title: Silver's sixth straight deficit year
trending.summary: The Silver Institute expects a 35-million-ounce silver deficit in 2026, the sixth straight shortfall, taking the cumulative gap since 2021 to about 746 million ounces.

trending.title: Indian jewellery volumes fall even as spending rises
trending.summary: Jewellery demand by volume fell 20% in the September quarter while its value rose 16%, and Diwali gold purchases rose 30% as prices fell 21%, with 52 tonnes sold.

trending.title: European central banks move gold out of US vaults
trending.summary: The Dutch central bank shifted about 86 tonnes of gold to London and France moved its last 129 tonnes from New York; BlackRock says gold and silver are more than defensive assets.

items.title: Gold rises on bargain hunting but heads for weekly decline
items.summary: Spot gold rose 1% to $3,915.31 an ounce on Friday as bargain hunting emerged after Thursday's slide to its lowest since October 2025, though it stayed down 3.5% for the week. Silver rose 1% to $50.49 an ounce, also headed for a weekly fall, as markets priced an 89% chance of a 25-basis-point December Fed hike and awaited US producer prices at 19:00 IST.

items.title: Gold inches higher but heads for weekly loss on Fed hike concerns
items.summary: Spot gold edged up 0.2% to $3,883 an ounce after Thursday's 3% slide to a more than one-year low, but stayed on course for a 4.4% weekly fall. Oil jumped after attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure and Hormuz shipping risks, stoking inflation fears, while Fed officials signalled further rises may be needed and markets priced an 85% chance of a December hike. Spot silver steadied at $50.07.

items.title: Dollar near 19-month high on Fed hike bets, yen tests 160
items.summary: The dollar held near a 19-month high on Friday as bets on a larger Fed rate rise grew, with the yen back near 160 per dollar and two-year Treasury yields up 34 basis points in two sessions. Traders now price a 14.5% chance of a 50-basis-point December hike, up from zero last week, after hot US inflation data and hawkish Fed remarks; the dollar index stood at 103.17.

items.title: Silver Market Set for Sixth Consecutive Annual Deficit in 2026
items.summary: The Silver Institute and Metals Focus expect the global silver market to run a 35-million-ounce deficit in 2026, the sixth straight year demand beats supply, taking the cumulative shortfall since 2021 to about 746 million ounces. Total demand is forecast at 1.08 billion ounces, down 5% on the year, while industrial demand outside solar is set to rise 4.5%.

items.title: Jewellers' strong Q2 growth masks a continued drop in gold volumes
items.summary: Organised jewellers reported strong revenue growth in the September quarter, but India's gold jewellery demand by volume fell 20% from a year earlier even as its value rose 16%, the World Gold Council says. Crisil expects retailer revenue to grow 21-23% in FY27 while volumes fall 4-6%, with gold prices averaging 25-27% higher than last year.

items.title: Gold falls to over one-year low below $3,900 amid inflation concerns, US PPI data looms
items.summary: Gold slipped to a more than one-year low near $3,880 in early Asian trade on Friday as persistent US inflation worries and expectations of higher rates weighed, with traders awaiting October US producer price data later in the day. Markets now see a 14.5% chance of a 50-basis-point December Fed hike, up from zero before Tuesday's CPI report; headline PPI is expected to rise 6.6% on the year.

items.title: Silver tumbles over 3% as hot US inflation boosts Fed hike bets
items.summary: Silver fell 3% on Thursday to about $50.15 an ounce as the dollar index neared 103.10, its highest since April 2025, and traders fully priced a December Fed rate rise. Core US CPI rose 0.3% in October, above forecasts, and hawkish remarks from Fed officials including Christopher Waller and Beth Hammack weighed on the metal; traders now await Friday's US producer price data.

items.title: SGB 2018-19 Series III final redemption today: Investors to earn up to 348% return; check RBI fixed price, interest rate
items.summary: The RBI has fixed the final redemption price for Sovereign Gold Bond 2018-19 Series-III at ₹14,024 per unit as the tranche matures on November 13, 2026, eight years after issue. Holders who bought at ₹3,183 a gram gain about 341%, and online buyers at ₹3,133 up to 348%, before the 2.5% annual interest.

items.title: India Bullion: Down as dollar hits 19-month high; hawkish Fed also weighs
items.summary: Gold and silver futures on MCX and COMEX fell for a third straight session as the dollar rose to a 19-month high above 103 and traders fully priced a December Fed rate rise. At 18:49 IST, MCX December gold stood at Rs 1,41,185 per 10 g and silver at Rs 1,80,800 per kg; jewellers cut domestic discounts to Rs 500 as lower prices drew buying, with the rupee at 94.04 per dollar.

items.title: Gold, silver extend losses as Fed hike bets lift dollar, Treasury yields
items.summary: Spot gold fell to $3,890.46 an ounce, down 2.38%, and silver to $50.19, down 2.8%, as hot October inflation and rising jobless claims kept a December Fed hike in focus. Traders put 88-91% odds on a 25-basis-point rise at the December 8-9 meeting, the 10-year yield traded near 5.00% and the dollar held near 102.85 after a 19-month high. Friday's October producer prices are the next test.

items.title: “We believe gold and silver are not simply defensive assets” – BlackRock’s Akullian
items.summary: BlackRock's Kristy Akullian says gold and silver still carry long-term structural support despite the pullback from January's record, with gold down about 10% so far this year after topping $5,000 an ounce. She casts gold as a portfolio diversifier and store of value, and silver as a higher-volatility metal backed by industrial demand from AI infrastructure, electrification and solar.

items.title: India's retail inflation rises to 6.09% in October, breaches RBI limit
items.summary: India's retail inflation rose to 6.09% in October from 5.54% in September, crossing the RBI's 6% upper tolerance limit for the first time under the new series, as food inflation climbed to 8.94% on onion prices up 116%. The print strengthens the case for another rate rise at the RBI's December 2-4 meeting, after the repo rate was raised to 5.50% in October.

items.title: Gold falls below ₹1.39 lakh per 10 grams, silver drops 1.3%: What’s driving the latest correction
items.summary: MCX gold slipped below ₹1.39 lakh per 10 g and silver fell 1.3% in the latest session, with December gold around ₹1,38,599 and silver near ₹1,82,110 per kg. CNBC-TV18 puts the slide down to a dollar at a 19-month high and traders fully pricing a December Fed rate rise after hot US inflation data.

items.title: Why European Central Banks Want Their Gold Back
items.summary: European central banks are moving gold out of US vaults, with the Dutch central bank shifting about 86 tonnes to London and France completing the move of 129 tonnes from New York so its full 2,437-tonne reserve sits in Paris. Banks cite crisis preparedness and liquidity, while central banks globally have bought about 1,000 tonnes a year since 2022, the World Gold Council says.

items.title: TD Securities sees gold retesting $3,900 as Fed hike bets and a firm dollar bite
items.summary: TD Securities expects gold to retest support near $3,900 an ounce as higher US rates and a firmer dollar weigh on investment demand, the bank's head of commodity strategy Bart Melek said, adding that central-bank buying below $4,000 may cushion the fall. TD still sees scope for record highs above $5,300 in 2027 once oil-driven inflation fades.

items.title: Gold, silver slide in India as Fed rate hike bets hit 100%, rupee offers little relief
items.summary: Gold and silver slid further: MCX gold fell 1.4% to Rs 1,37,755 per 10 g and silver 1.69% to Rs 1,81,400 per kg. CME FedWatch puts a December Fed rise at 100% - about 91% for 25 basis points and 9.2% for 50 - after hot October US inflation and hawkish Fed remarks lifted the dollar index briefly above 103 and the 10-year US yield near 5%. The rupee, at Rs 93.8075, offered little relief.

items.title: Gold Prices Fall By Rs 1,300 To Below Rs 1,39,000; Silver Rates Slump By Rs 2,800
items.summary: December gold futures fell Rs 1,216 to Rs 1,38,500 per 10 g and silver Rs 2,775 to Rs 1,81,750 per kg as the dollar climbed to a 19-month high. Markets are now fully pricing a December Fed rate rise and another in March 2027 after hot October US inflation and hawkish Fed remarks. Gold ETF inflows fell 22% month on month to Rs 3,470 crore in October.

items.title: US Fed sets new meeting schedule for 2027, as foretold by Chairman Kevin Warsh
items.summary: The Federal Reserve has published its 2027 meeting calendar, naming the November 16-17 session as a monetary policy strategy meeting with no rate vote and no policy statement, as Chairman Kevin Warsh announced in October. The Fed will hold seven rate-setting meetings in 2027 and six in 2028, keeping eight meetings a year, with the rest devoted to strategy. The calendar was updated on November 12.

items.title: Silver Falls as Rising Real Yields Overshadow Supply Deficits
items.summary: Silver fell 3.9% to $51.32 an ounce on Tuesday as rising real yields overshadowed a fifth straight year of structural supply deficits, the Silver Institute's data shows. The 10-year real yield rose to 2.78% from 2.63% the previous week, leaving rallies capped below $55, FXEmpire's analysis says.

items.title: Silver Price Outlook: Positioning In Gold, Silver Turned Light Says JP Morgan
items.summary: Spot silver eased to about $51.03 an ounce on Thursday, after a 3.48% drop on Tuesday, as JP Morgan's metals and mining team said investor positioning in gold and silver has turned light. Non-commercial traders held a net 21,251 COMEX silver contracts long on November 3, up 1,548 in a week.

items.title: Gold purchases rose 30% as prices fell 21%: 52 tonnes of gold worth ₹72,000 crore sold during Diwali-Dhanteras; silver purchases also rose 10%
items.summary: Gold buying rose 30% by volume during Dhanteras and Diwali compared with last year, the India Bullion and Jewellers Association says, with about 52 tonnes worth ₹72,000 crore sold and silver purchases up 10% to 300 tonnes worth ₹5,400 crore. The rebound followed a price correction from about ₹1.8 lakh to ₹1.42 lakh per 10 g, with jewellers also citing advance wedding-season buying.

items.title: Precious Metals Attract Rs 6,566 Cr; Gold ETF Inflows Fall 22%, Silver ETFs See 56% Surge
items.summary: Indian precious-metals ETFs drew about Rs 6,566 crore in October, AMFI data show: gold ETF inflows fell nearly 22% to Rs 3,474.03 crore from September's Rs 4,450.61 crore, while silver ETF inflows jumped over 56% to Rs 3,092.22 crore. Gold ETFs have taken in about Rs 49,399 crore in January-October 2026, already more than all of 2025.

items.title: Gold ETF inflows beat full-year 2025 total in just 10 months, cross Rs 49,000 crore
items.summary: Indian gold ETFs drew Rs 49,399 crore in the first ten months of 2026, already about Rs 6,400 crore more than the Rs 42,961 crore they took in during all of 2025, Moneycontrol reports from AMFI data. October inflows slowed after September's quarter-end bunching, but the ten-month total still set a record.

items.title: India Gold Demand 2026: Why Are Indians Buying Less Gold?
items.summary: India's gold demand fell 12% to 443.9 tonnes in January-September 2026, with jewellery demand down 18% to 241.1 tonnes, as record prices and the May import-duty hike curbed buying, Business Outreach reports from World Gold Council data. Full-year demand is estimated at about 650 tonnes, the lowest since 2020, while gold ETF inflows rose 47%.

items.title: India Needs Better Gold Mining Evaluation: NITI Aayog CEO
items.summary: NITI Aayog chief executive Anurag Jain called for a proper evaluation matrix for awarding gold exploration and mining projects, PTI reports, to build technical competence and cut India's import dependence. A meeting on the Pahle India Foundation report cited geological data gaps, limited exploration, long project timelines and auction design as hurdles.
